title: Boundary maps for square-zero ring extensions are derivations
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let O' \to O be a surjection of sheaves of commutative O_X-algebras with square-zero kernel I. Since I^2=0, multiplication by local sections of O' on I factors through O, so I is an O-module and H^1(X,I) has the induced H^0(X,O)-module structure. For the connecting map partial: H^0(X,O) \to H^1(X,I) [pqf-def-cohomology] of 0 \to I \to O' \to O \to 0, one has partial(fg) = f partial(g) + g partial(f) for all f,g in H^0(X,O).

proof.text: Because I^2=0, the action of a local section of O' on I depends only on its image in O: changing a lift by an element of I changes the product by an element of I^2. Thus I is an O-module, and multiplication by a global section of O is an endomorphism of the O_X-module I. The sequence 0 -> I -> O' -> O -> 0 is a short exact sequence of O_X-modules, so [pqf-def-cohomology] supplies its long exact cohomology sequence, and applying the functor H^1(X,-) to these endomorphisms gives the H^0(X,O)-module structure on H^1(X,I).
The connecting map in the long exact cohomology sequence is additive, so it remains to prove the Leibniz identity for products.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 0B8S proof, sentence 'The boundary map is additive hence it suffices to prove the Leibniz rule'

proof.text: For f in H^0(X,O), choose a cover U_i and lifts f_i in O'(U_i). By [lem-sc-boundary-cech-local-lifts], the differences alpha_{i_0 i_1}=f_{i_0}-f_{i_1} form a Cech 1-cocycle in I and represent partial(f) under the injective Cech-to-H^1 map. After refining the cover, choose lifts g_i of a second section g; the same node identifies the Cech classes of beta_{i_0 i_1}=g_{i_0}-g_{i_1} and gamma_{i_0 i_1}=f_{i_0}g_{i_0}-f_{i_1}g_{i_1} with partial(g) and partial(fg).

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 0B8S proof, local lifts and the Cech classes alpha, beta, gamma

proof.text: On each overlap, the elementary identity f_{i_0}g_{i_0}-f_{i_1}g_{i_1}=(f_{i_0}-f_{i_1})g_{i_0}+f_{i_1}(g_{i_0}-g_{i_1})=(f_{i_0}-f_{i_1})g+f(g_{i_0}-g_{i_1}) holds in I because the two factors that differ by an element of I have the same image in O and I^2=0. Therefore gamma=alpha·g+f·beta in the Cech complex, where alpha·g and f·beta are obtained by applying the endomorphisms 'multiplication by g' and 'multiplication by f' of I to the cocycles. By [lem-sc-cech-h1-map-natural] the canonical map from Cech cohomology to H^1(X,I) carries the classes of alpha·g and f·beta to g partial(f) and f partial(g), so the identifications of step 3 give partial(fg)=g partial(f)+f partial(g).
